## I4 functional architecture

```text
ordinary bridge order_data ----\
                                -> prebuild-priority mux
R01 prebuild order_data --------/          |
                                           v
                                  shared futures risk
                                  - atomic CL admission
                                  - committed EX
                                  - one state owner
                                  - one AMU owner
                                           |
                                     ACCEPT only
                                           v
                              frozen financial_protocol_encoder
                                           |
                                          R01
```

`ENABLE_R01_PREBUILD=1` in the frozen XGMII-oriented baseline means the prebuild path must be gated; ordinary-bridge-only interception is not acceptable.

## Corrected frozen-AMU contract

The first local real-AMU parity run compiled/elaborated and produced all 80 baseline R01 bytes, but the integrated path produced zero bytes and held a risk reject. Root cause was not the frozen encoder or the two Codex local test edits. It was an HFT_RMIC integration contract bug:

```text
Frozen AMU new INSERT success:
rsp_ok     = 1
rsp_status = OK
rsp_found  = 0
```

The prior CI stub incorrectly used `found=1` for a new INSERT, and CL admission therefore required `found=1`. The actual AMU successfully inserted the order, after which integration falsely treated the response as failure, rolled the reservation back and rejected the order.

Corrected head now:

- accepts new INSERT on `ok && status==OK`;
- reproduces real INSERT/duplicate/UPDATE semantics in the CI AMU stub;
- verifies newly inserted/updated context through LOOKUP;
- reruns committed execution, atomic admission, shared-core and dual-source regressions on the corrected contract;
- preserves Codex's useful Windows log-lock and bounded-timeout ideas, with fail-fast reject diagnostics in parity TB;
- records the I3 physical-result claim correction in `docs/results/i3_atomic_cl2ex_ooc_postroute.md` and `D-20260918-14`.

## Remaining I4 local gates

After discarding the two superseded local Codex edits and pulling this branch, run in this order:

```powershell
pwsh .\scripts\run_i4_r01_parity_xsim.ps1
pwsh .\scripts\run_i4_r01_path_ooc_impl.ps1
```

The parity runner now avoids Windows native-log file locking and packages PASS/FAIL evidence. Its TB immediately reports risk reject source/code instead of hanging until a generic timeout.

The OOC flow uses the corrected admission predicate, real pinned RMIC XPM AMU, shared futures state, dual-source order boundary and pinned frozen HFT encoder. Acceptance remains full route at 6.400 ns with real BRAM, WNS >= 0, TNS = 0, zero routing errors, and reviewed utilization/DRC/power/critical path.
